answer: Epochal verifiable delay functions resist a tide of fake AI agents by requiring each public key to compute a sequential modular-squaring chain from a fresh randomness beacon and submit a succinct proof. Because the seed binds the key, clones cannot echo a shared output; each active identity incurs the verifiable cost of dedicating sequential compute and energy over the epoch time delta. Still, adversaries deploying custom low-latency ASICs can batch multiple identities within one window.
